abstract: We investigate the relative value of labeled and unlabeled samples in constructing classification rules. We observe a training set Q composed of l labeled and u unlabeled samples coming from two classes. Let sample from class 1 be distributed according to f/sub 1/(/spl middot/), samples from class 2 according to f/sub 2/(/spl middot/), and let /spl eta/ be the probability that a sample is in class 1. Assume that f/sub 1/(/spl middot/) and f/sub 2/(/spl middot/) are known and that /spl eta/ is unknown. We want to classify a new sample X/sub 0/. The relative value of labeled and unlabeled observations in reducing the probability of error is equal to I/sub t/(/spl eta/)/I/sub u/(/spl eta/), the ratio of the Fisher information of the labeled and unlabeled samples. Moreover labeled samples are not necessary in order to construct a decision rule. However, if f/sub 1/(/spl middot/) and f/sub 2/(/spl middot/) are given, but it is not known whether observations from class 1 are distributed according to f/sub 1/(/spl middot/) or according to f/sub 2/(/spl middot/), then the labeled samples are necessary and exponentially more valuable than unlabeled samples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On single-user decodable codes for the Gaussian multiple access channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: It is shown that any rate tuple R contained in the capacity region of the Gaussian multiple access channel can be achieved by means of multiple access codes with decoding complexity equivalent to that of at most 2m-1 single-user codes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive universal variable-to-fix lossless coding scheme
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We suggest an adaptive, universal variable-to-fix (VF) lossless source coding technique which generates a dictionary that is sequentially adapted to the empirical distribution of the data observed so far. Since the dictionary varies, we also provide an algorithm to implement the VF code without an explicit specification of the dictionary, and so there is no need for dictionary storage. For i.i.d sources our algorithm converges to the entropy at a rate O(l/logM)+O(logn/n), where M is the dictionary size and a is the length of the sequence to be compressed. The adaptive dictionary construction algorithm has some resemblance to arithmetic coding.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bounds on R(D) for an AR(1) Gaussian source with parameter uncertainty
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The rate distortion theory of Gaussian autoregressive (AR) sources is relatively well understood. However it is often the case that we do not know the exact parameters of the AR source parameters. The present authors are interested in obtaining upper and lower bounds on the rate distortion function R(D) for a Gaussian AR(1) source subject to the mean square error fidelity criterion for a given range of model parameter uncertainty.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the asymptotic performance of the generalized Viterbi algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The expurgated bound is extended to the generalised Viterbi algorithm (GVA) over the binary input AWGN channel and is shown to agree well with the simulation result. Moreover, we show that the expurgate bound for the GVA is also exact at zero-rate for uncorrelated codes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Subfield-level decoding of Reed-Solomon codes based on coordinate codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Based on the algebraic structure of subfield-expanded Reed-Solomon codes, we discuss a parallel decoding algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sequential multihypothesis testing and nonuniform costs with applications in hybrid serial search
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A sequential multihypothesis test designed for use with nonuniform decision costs is presented and its performance is characterized. Asymptotic efficiency of the test is shown, and the use of sequential multihypothesis tests in hybrid serial search schemes is discussed. A generalisation of the M-ary sequential probability ratio test is considered for the decision making problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coding, processing gain, and modulation in frequency-hopped multiple access communications: tradeoff considerations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We consider a situation where K transmitter-receiver pairs communicate simultaneously over a channel of bandwidth B. Each transmitter sends one of the M possible signals in every 2 seconds over one of the p possible frequency slots, having a bandwidth of B/q. We assume the use of M-ary FSK orthogonal signaling with noncoherent detection. Each transmitter-receiver pair has a unique hopping pattern that selects the frequency slot. We model the hopping patterns as independent, identically distributed (i.i.d.) random sequences uniformly distributed over a set of q frequencies. We assume that each packet consists of a Reed-Solomon (RS) codeword, and one code symbol (M-ary) is transmitted per hop.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Four non-existence results for ternary linear codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: It is proved that ternary codes with parameters [15,8,6], [15,9,5], [16,6,8], and [16,7,7] do not exist. This result solves the problem of finding optimal ternary codes of length at most 21. Also some uniqueness results are derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Approximate ML-estimates of random processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Computationally feasible versions of maximum likelihood estimations (MLEs), called approximate MLEs (AMLEs), are introduced. Estimation models with all, some, or no AMLEs consistent are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On noncoherent detection of noisy phase OOK signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper considers the use of noncoherent detection using L-fold square-law combining for binary On Off Keying (OOK) modulation in a noisy phase channel. The channel presents both additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) as well as Brownian phase noise. Approximating the unknown distribution law of the underlying phase functionals by a class of discrete distributions, we obtain an analytic expression for the BER of noisy phase OOK signals detected with square-law combining. The discrete distribution laws support any given number of power moments admitted by the phase functionals. These moments are exactly known and are given in closed form analytic expressions. The particular distribution laws chosen here are a pair called principal representations from the theory of Tchebycheff-Systems. The above numerical methods are used to investigate the dependence of the BER on the following parameters: decision threshold, IF bandwidth, the bit energy to noise spectral density ratio (E/sub b//N/sub 0/) and the Brownian phase 3 dB linewidth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance bounds and cutoff rates of quantum limited OOK with optical amplification
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The bit error probability (BER) and generalized cutoff rate (GCR) of optically amplified, direct-detection on-off keying (OOK) signaling is addressed, utilizing the classical theory of Fredholm integral equations. The approach accounts for the impact of optical bandlimiting in the Poisson regime and upper bounds on the BER are found via Chernoff techniques which address the resultant intersymbol interference (ISI) incurred by the linear pulse dispersion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Decoding algebraic-geometric codes using Grobner bases
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Developments in coding theory have seen two ideas for generalizing Reed-Solomon codes to obtain better codes: multidimensional cyclic (MDC) coder, and algebraic-geometric (AG) codes. In MDC codes, polynomials in several variables take the place of univariate polynomials. In AG codes, the concept of a polynomial in one variable is generalized to a rational function on an algebraic curve. Grobner bases have proved to be a useful tool both in the theory of multivariate polynomials, and in computations involving them. Therefore it is natural that they play an central role in decoding algorithms for MDC and AG codes. We present two decoding algorithms based on Grobner bases which generalize well-known algorithms for decoding Reed-Solomon codes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A construction method for unidirectional error control codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A construction method for systematic t-UEC d-UED codes is proposed. These are codes that are able to simultaneously correct up to t unidirectional errors and detect from t+1 up to d unidirectional errors. Complexity as well as efficiency issues are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Several classes of generalized concatenated codes for byte error-control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We propose classes of generalized concatenated codes for byte error-control. Generalized concatenated codes have been proposed by Zinov'ev. The classes proposed here contain not only linear codes but also nonlinear codes. We also have simple modifications from the codes described to byte error-locating codes such as Fujiwara-Kitakami codes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of partial response coded MPSK over mobile satellite channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We consider the partial response signaling for M-ary phase shift keying (MPSK) modulation transmitted over mobile satellite channels in the presence of fading and white Gaussian noise. The bit error probability upper bounds are derived for both the partial response coded and uncoded MPSK cases. One interesting result, obtained from the comparison, is that the partial response coded MPSK outperforms the uncoded MPSK in the fading environment for signal-to-noise ratio values greater than a threshold, when the soft decision Viterbi decoder is used, in contrast to the AWGN channels. Computer simulations done for the Rayleigh fading case, also verify this aspect of the partial response signaling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the trellis complexity of composite-length cyclic codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The trellis complexity of block codes is closely related to their soft-decision decoding complexity. We investigate the trellis properties of composite-length cyclic codes. Trellis-oriented decompositions are presented, and improved upper bounds on the trellis complexity are derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trace description of q-ary linear codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: J. Wolfmann (see A.A.E.C.C., vol.2, p.119, 1991) gives a description of projective binary linear codes by means of a polynomial. The purpose of our work is first to generalize such a description to q-ary codes. Then the main difficulty is to evaluate the weights of these codes and it is not possible to follow the same method as in the binary case. We consider Artin-Schreier curves and we give a bound on weights. Some normalization are also investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The accuracy of estimating the parameters of stationary processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Addresses the general problem of establishing bounds on the achievable estimation accuracy of the parameters of a regular stationary process, from a single observed realization of this process. The special case of establishing bounds on the estimation accuracy of the parameters of harmonic components in the presence of noise with a known spectrum or covariance function has been studied quite extensively, especially for the case in which the noise is white. However, relatively little work seems to have been done for the case of harmonic components in unknown noise. The authors concentrate on a solution to the problem of the achievable accuracy in jointly estimating the parameters of the harmonic (deterministic) and purely indeterministic components of the process, based on a finite length, single observed realization of this process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On parameter estimation for quantum processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. A comparative discussion of three basic procedures of continuous quantum measurement for estimating parameters of quantum stochastic processes is presented. Quantum stochastic process is one-parameter family of (vector) operators in a Hilbert space, together with a density operator, defining quantum state. If the density operator depends on unknown parameters, one may speak of the parameter estimation from quantum measurements of the process. The fundamental difficulty of the quantum case is that components of the process may not commute, and a measurement at some time will introduce specific quantum disturbances at later times. Its resolution requires the new concept of quantum measurement, continuous in time. Three basic procedures are described: quantum nondemolition (QND), quantum demolition (QD), and extended quantum nondemolition (EQND) measurements. It is shown that statistical inference based on QND and QD leads to estimates which are in general only suboptimal, while EQND reaches fundamental limitations imposed by the quantum Cramer-Rao inequality. The argument is based on physically motivated examples and leads to possible implementation of the discussed measurement procedures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On block coded ARQ schemes cumulating the rejected sequences
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We show that the received sequences, which are rejected and not discarded on ARQ schemes, make the next decision with repeat request powerful by a random coding arguments. We first give the ordinary ARQ of the basic algorithm with some criterion, and define the ARQ with cumulating the rejected sequences, which naturally extended from the ordinary one. Then we study the error exponent of decoding the second received sequences under the condition that the first is rejected. We assume the block coded ARQ with noiseless feedback.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On restoration of band-limited signals from noisy observations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We consider the problem of restoration of band-limited functions from noisy observations. The algorithms are proposed and their convergence properties investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Block arithmetic coding and error correcting coding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We discuss the combination of block arithmetic coding (BAC), a technique for entropy compression, and error correcting coding. In essence, this is a joint source-channel coding problem. BAC is used to entropy code the input sequence and ordinary linear block codes are used to combat channel errors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On lattice quantization noise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present several results regarding the spectral properties and the divergence from Gaussianity of a random vector, uniformly distributed over a lattice cell.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Redundancy rates for renewal and other processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The paper addresses the theoretical issue of universal noiseless source coding, viz., the best possible redundancy bound achievable for a given class of source models by block to variable-length lossless coding. For parametric model classes such as memoryless or Markov sources, this bound grows as the log of the block-length n, [1,2,4]. The authors show that for the non-parametric class of renewal processes the growth rate is O(square root n), while for the class of Markov renewal processes of order k the rate is O(n/sup k+1/k+2/). <<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Soft-decision multistage decoding of multilevel-coded quaternary partial-response signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper deals with multilevel coding and concatenated soft-decision multistage decoding for quaternary dicode partial-response systems. Time-interleaved quaternary symbols are transmitted with precoding over the dicode channel. A single level of coding is assumed, whereby only the less significant bits of the transmitted quaternary symbols are encoded. In the receiver, an inner decoder computes approximate log-likelihood ratios for the less significant bits of the quaternary symbols input to the precoded partial-response channel by a new, reduced two-state, soft-output Viterbi decoding algorithm. With sufficient interleaving, the log-likelihood ratios represent the appropriate metrics for soft-decision decoding by an outer multistage decoder. Real coding gains over uncoded transmission with optimum maximum-likelihood sequence decoding were determined by simulation. Results are presented for various multilevel coder based on binary convolutional or Reed-Muller block codes. This scheme exhibits low decoding complexity and allows high-rate codes that achieve real coding gains of 3 to 4 dB.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New upper bounds on the covering radius of codes with known dual distance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Using the linear programming approach and the concept of weighted coverings we derive new upper bounds on the covering radius of codes with a given cardinality and a given dual distance. There has been a recent revival of interest in the problem of finding upper bounds on the covering radius of a code as a function of its size, dual distance or minimal distance. This problem relates to some methods of coding for write-once memories, interconnection networks, quantization, etc. If we assume that the minimal distance of a linear code is greater than 3 then the problem corresponds to evaluating the diameter of a subclass of Cayley graphs over Z/sub 2//sup r/ of given degree and robustness.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a multi-D trellis decoder for a 155 Mbit/s concatenated codec
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: An implementation of a 16 state, rate 8/9 six-dimensional (6-D) 8PSK rotationally invariant trellis decoder for use in a concatenated codec is described, The concatenated codec allows transmission of STM-1 signals (at the 155.52 Mbit's information rate) over a 72 MHz satellite transponder. The inner trellis decoder is used with an outer (255,239) Reed-Solomon (RS) block decoder. The trellis decoder operates at 165.93 Mbit/s and currently has an implementation loss of only 0.2 dB. The concatenated codec achieves a bit error ratio of 10/sup -10/ at an E/sub b/N/sub 0/ of 8.2 dB (assuming an ideal modem and AWGN channel).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bounds for the computation of the free distance of codes based on convolution
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper presents new bounds to be used in the search for the free distance (D/sub free/) of infinite response codes based on filtering a PAM modulated signal. The bounds extend the two main criteria used to prune paths with trellis codes, namely: path weight comparisons: from each state only the path with the smallest weight is extended; and bounding: if the weight is larger than an upper bound on D/sub free/ then no path is extended. If a PAM signal is filtered with an IIR filter, then we have a linear tree code, and the paths do not merge. In addition, the weight D/sub free/ is reached only in the limit. We show that, by using more powerful bounds, it is possible to compare paths in the cases of "near merges," and to find when a path corresponds to D/sub free/ in early stages of the search. The new bounds are useful for several types of convolutional coding, and for that reason we present a quite general approach, and exemplify the solutions for filtered PAM and also for binary convolutional codes (BCC).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low-complexity trellis decoding of linear block codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A new encoding technique which allows the design of a wide variety of block codes is introduced. Based on this technique, minimal trellises of the codes are designed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of a square-law combiner for reception of Nakagami fading orthogonal signals in spherically invariant noise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The performance of a square-law combiner for diversity reception of M-ary orthogonal signaling subject to flat-flat Nakagami fading and spherically invariant noise (SIN) is evaluated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synchronization performance for direct-carrier-modulation at low data-rates
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The residual-carrier synchronization performance of a phase-locked loop is analysed for the case of low data-rate, channel encoded applications with direct-carrier-modulation, avoiding the use of subcarriers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A rigorous analysis of Linsker's Hebbian learning network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We propose a novel approach for a rigorous analysis of the nonlinear asymmetric dynamics of Linsker's (1986) unsupervised Hebbian learning network. The results provide for the first time comprehensive explanations of the origin of the various structured connection patterns and of the roles of the different system parameters of the model. Our theoretical predictions are corroborated by numerical simulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bounds on the minimum distance of the duals of BCH codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We consider duals of BCH codes of length p/sup m/-1 over GF(p). A lower bound on their minimum distance is found via the adaptation of the Weil bound to cyclic codes. However, this bound is of no significance for roughly half of these codes. We partially fill this gap by giving a lower bound for an infinite class of duals of BCH codes. We also present a lower bound obtained with an algorithm due to Massey and Schaub (1988). In the case of binary codes of length 127 and 255, the results are surprisingly higher than all previously known bounds.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Matrix product-form solutions with application to queueing theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We study a discrete time bivariate Markov chain {(X/sub /spl xi//, N/sub /spl xi//), /spl xi//spl ges/0} in which the values of X/sub /spl xi// are represented by the nodes of a d-ary tree, and N/sub /spl xi// takes integer values between 1 and m. When d equals 1, our results reduce to the theory of matrix-geometric solutions developed by Neuts (1981).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Information and control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Summary form only given. The main theme of the article is to discuss how to associate a value with information in the context of control. It concludes with a discussion of some differences between control and communication. Two issues are time delays and computational requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Almost sure waiting time results for weak and very weak Bernoulli processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Asymptotic properties of the waiting time W/sub k/(x, y) until an initial segment of length k of a sample path x of an ergodic finite-alphabet process is seen in an independently chosen sample path y were discussed in earlier papers by Wyner and Ziv (1985), by Noble and Wyner (see IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, vol.IT-38, p.1551, 1993), and by Shields (see The Journal of Theoretical Probability, vol.6, p.499-519, 1993). These results are sharpened to obtain almost sure convergence in the weak Bernoulli case for exact matches and in the very weak Bernoulli case for approximate matches. The weak Bernoulli proof uses recent results obtained by the authors about estimation of joint distributions, while the very weak Bernoulli result utilizes a new characterization of such processes in terms of a blowing-up property.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Second order stationary models for 1/f processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A subclass of statistically self-similar processes with correlation structure of the form E[X(t)X(t/spl lambda/)]=R(/spl lambda/) is considered. A spectral decomposition theorem for such processes is stated. Based on linear scale-invariant system theory, scale invariant autoregressive processes are developed. The proposed models are intuitive, mathematically simple and practical candidates for modeling 1/f processes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A lower bound on the probability of erasure for an anti-jamming code when used on the binary OR-channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: An anti-jamming code consists of a set of codes obtained from the coset partitioning of a larger code. The code is used over a binary OR-channel subject to intentional interference. We derive a lower bound on the probability of erasing a codeword.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sequential sequence estimation for CPM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A major disadvantage of CPM is the complexity of the optimal receiver. The number of states in the trellis repesentation are on the order of M/sup L/, where M is the modulation alphabet size and L the memory imposed by the modulation scheme. Here we investigate the reduction of the graph search by using a sequential search.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of frequency domain delay and multiply receivers for spread spectrum modulated signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Prefilter delay and multiply (PFDM) devices have been shown to be useful in clock recovery and signal detection. This is of particular interest in spread spectrum modulated signals of unknown chip rate whose presence must be detected. The PFDM receiver is well suited to this task. The overall performance and utility of the FDDM receiver (the PFDM frequency domain counterpart) is compared and contrasted with known (or simulated) performance results associated with PFDM devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On L/sub 2/ convergence rates of radial basis function networks and kernel regression estimators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The paper generalises the rates of L/sub 2/ convergence for RBF nets based on the kernel regression estimates (KRE) obtained by optimising the empirical error with respect to the weight vector and the receptive field size. The centers of the radial functions are placed at the points sampled with replacement from the learning sequence. The bounded output convergence and the rate of convergence for the RBF net have been obtained for radial functions with noncompact support. New results have been obtained for the L/sub 2/ convergence rates of KRE and RBF nets in the case of unbounded outputs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of array output processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Representations are given for the array output due to a nonGaussian random field of a general class. Applications are given to signal detection and to channel capacity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of a class of geometrically designed trellis codes for M-PSK
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A class of trellis codes is introduced based on a novel trellis structure. Codes are constructed by mapping coefficient sets onto branches in the trellis. Sets are given an algebraic structure by operations in a ring which will generate a rich class of codes and allow linear codes to be defined. Current interest is in finding codes with good performance and a reasonably large data rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Lower bounds on the cross-correlation for codes of a given size
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The best known lower bounds on the cross-correlation of real and complex codes of a given size obtained by the author in 1982 are investigated. For a certain range of parameters these bounds are strengthened. Their optimality in the framework of the linear programming method for polynomials of bounded degree is proved. New asymptotics for the code size growing polynomially in length are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RLL (d,k) coding using structured vector quantization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Run-length-limited (RLL) codes, also known as (d,k) RLL codes, are typically used in high-density digital magnetic recording systems to increase the recording density and control self clocking. We design encoders that map unconstrained information binary sequences into (d, k) RLL constrained sequences. A direct approach to the design of encoders and decoders for our RLL codes can be realized using some ideas from the fixed-rate structured vector quantizer. We show that this approach is well suited to shift, insertion and deletion error correction. For the multistage approach, we prove that our code can be encoded and decoded using p simple parallel codes realized using the same idea. We show also that we can incorporate easily multilevel coding with multistage decoding in the multistage RLL encoder/decoder. We show also that, for both direct and multistage approaches, the optimum thresholds of our RLL code are modified when error-correcting codes are inserted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A coding theoretic approach to attack certain stream ciphers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present a coding theoretic approach to the problem the initial state recovery of a linear feedback shift register when a noisy output sequence is given. Our work is focused on the investigation of the asymptotical behaviour of the recovery process. We give two algorithms which will work for shift registers with arbitrary feedback polynomial. Furthermore, the number of required given noisy symbols is close to its lower limit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new construction for n-track (d, k) codes with redundancy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Digital magnetic and optical storage systems employing NRZI recording use (d, k) codes. The d-parameter specifies the minimum number of 0's occurring between 1's while the k-parameter specifies the maximum number of 0's between l's. The n-track (d,k) codes (denoted as (d,k;n) codes) are extensions of (d, k) codes for use in multiple-track systems. Instead of imposing each track to individually satisfy both constraints, (d,k;n) codes satisfy the d-constraint in each track individually while relaxing the k-constraint by allowing it to be satisfied jointly by the multiple tracks. Although (d,k;n) codes can provide significant capacity increases over (d, k) codes, they suffer from the fact that a single faulty track can cause loss of synchronization and hence, loss of the data on all tracks. Orcutt and Marcellin (see IEEE Trans. on Inform. Theory, Sept., 1993) introduced n-track (d,k) codes with a redundancy of r (denoted as (d,k;n,r) codes) which allow for r faulty tracks by mandating that all subsets of n-r tracks satisfy the joint k-constraint. We propose a new method to construct (d,k; n, r) codes. These codes have simple encoding and decoding schemes, gain a large part of the capacity increase possible when using (d,k; n,r) codes, and are considerably more robust to faulty tracks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic threshold detection for maximum likelihood sequence estimation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Maximum likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) provides optimum detection for intersymbol interference (ISI) channels with additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). This decoding process dynamically searches the minimum path through the ISI channel trellis, using the Viterbi algorithm. We exploit the structure of this trellis and present an equivalent optimum scheme based on dynamic quantization, which reduces the computational complexity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Decomposition and construction of group codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A decomposition of a group code into a normal subcode and a quotient code can be characterized as group extension (extension code) of the subcode and the quotient code. Simple necessary and sufficient conditions are given for the existence of an extension code with given sub- and quotient code. These purely algebraic results are complemented by a characterization of finitely generated, complete, k-controllable group codes by a sublength-generation property of finite-length generators. This property leads to a new construction process of canonical minimal encoders.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient skew codes constructions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In communication channels consisting of many parallel sub-channels operating synchronously, the retrieval of data from all sub-channels form the message. Data can arrive at different times from the different sub-channels and it is possible that data from the next message is received before the completion of the current message. Skew detecting and tolerant codes can be used in such cases. We propose more efficient skew codes and introduce lower bounds on the number of the required check bits. The necessary and sufficient conditions for (t,d)-SD-codes are stated in the theorem given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Shared buffering in nonblocking copy networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of nonblocking copy networks employing the shared buffering scheme. We use the technique of tagged Markov chains to derive the stationary distributions for the occupancy of the buffers. Based on these stationary distributions, the delay, throughput, and packet loss probability are calculated as critical performance measures of the copy network. We also carry out analyses for variations in the copying policy such as fanout splitting wherein a copy request from a single packet may be completed over two time slots, and feed channel priority wherein there exists a certain priority among input channels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Noncoherent reception of multi-h signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Error performance of multi-h signals in noncoherent transmission over AWGN channels is presented. A comparison between multi-h and CPFSK signals is made for both coherent and noncoherent detection. This is done by means of an equivalent Euclidean distance. The achieved results are verified by simulation, using a VA algorithm for coherent detection and SAN(B) for noncoherent detection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimum detectors for PPM signals in airborne/underwater optical communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We develop a maximum likelihood optimum demodulation scheme for direct optical detection of PPM signals used in airborne/underwater communications. We use the irradiance of an optical pulse propagating through clear air and sea water derived using radiative transport theory. This hybrid optical channel is characterized by intersymbol and interslot interference.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Upper bounds and Hamming spheres under the DC-constraint
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Upper Hamming bounds are derived for the asymptotic rates R of DC-free binary codes with imbalances 3, 4 and 5. For large enough fractional distances /spl delta/, we derive an improved Plotkin bound, given by the straight line that contains the cutoff point (R=0, /spl delta/=.5) and is tangent to the Hamming bound.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Channel adaptive coding techniques through application of higher order moments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We investigate the use of higher order code word moments to shape the power spectral density of codes. Several codes are presented that combine different spectral shaping techniques. The insertion/deletion and additive error correcting capabilities of these codes are investigated and simple decoding procedures are presented. Finally, we give an example for the use of a higher order spectral zero code.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: P/sup 2/ codes: pragmatic trellis codes utilizing punctured convolutional codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A pragmatic approach to trellis codes is described whereby the core of the trellis decoder is a Viterbi decoder for punctured versions of the de facto standard, rate 1/2, 64, convolutional code.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ambiguity of integer sequences and application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present an algorithm which solves in polynomial time the problem of the ambiguity of integer sequences. This is done by introducing a suitable transformation from F/sub 2//sup n/ to {-1,0,1}/sup n/ and by the search of a short vector in a reduced lattice according to the L/sup 3/ algorithm. The algorithm presented shows that the Damgard (1989) hash function is insecure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Canonical m-sequences and dual basis generation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: An expression for the shift necessary to obtain a canonical m-sequence is obtained in terms of the coefficients of the primitive polynomial that generates this m-sequence. This is also directly related to the shift to obtain the location of the span '100...0' in the m-sequence. In addition it is shown how to recursively obtain the dual basis elements of the basis expressing GF(q/sup m/) over GF(q).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the decoding delay of encoders for input-constrained channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We show that checking whether there is a finite state encoder having local anticipation t encoding n-ary data into a constrained system S is a decidable problem. We also show that if there is such an encoder, then a version of the state-splitting algorithm can be applied to produce a finite state encoder having local anticipation at most 2t.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of the lattice sequence estimator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In many practical communication systems such as digital microwave radio, the main cause of transmission errors is usually due to the presence of intersymbol interference, rather than the noise. For such systems the sequence estimator significantly outperforms the symbol-by-symbol detector, even when a certain form of equalization techniques is used. The key obstacle to the applicability of sequence estimator is its large complexity. Denote the channel memory length by /spl nu/ and alphabet size by m. Using a Viterbi-like implementation, the estimator with truncation depth /spl delta/ requires O(m/sup /spl nu/+1/) arithmetic operations per symbol, and O(/spl delta/m/sup /spl nu//) storage elements. In most practical situations, /spl delta/ is chosen such that /spl delta/=O(/spl nu/). We propose the lattice sequence estimator (LSE), which only requires O(/spl delta/)/sup 2/ arithmetic operations per symbol, and O(/spl delta/) storage elements. For simplicity, the multilevel PAM system is considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Group codes defined on posets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The present paper is devoted to the study of group codes defined on posets. Their natural state realizations are introduced and shown to be minimal. The trellis diagrams of the natural state realizations are also studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of multiple access protocols in multihop networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Discusses the use of the busy tone multiple access (BTMA) protocol in multihop networks. The paper extends the analysis of Takagi and Kleinrock (1984) and provides the long run average throughput from the hidden Markov model. The performances of conservative BTMA and idealistic destination based BTMA. Multichannel CSMA and BTMA protocols are also discussed for the multihop networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiple insertion/deletion correcting codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The binary number theoretic single bit insertion or deletion correcting codes as pioneered by Levenshtein (1965) are investigated and some properties are presented. By extending these properties we present a generalized construction technique for binary codes that are able to correct multiple insertions/deletions of binary symbols.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Localized random and arbitrary errors in the light of AV channel theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A central problem in coding theory consists in finding bounds for the maximal size, say N(n,2t+1,q), of a t-error correcting code over a q-ary alphabet with blocklength n. This code concept is suited for communication over a q-ary channel with input and output alphabet X={0,1,...,q-1}, when a word of length n sent by the encoder is changed by the channel in at most t letters. Neither the encoder nor the decoder knows in advance where the errors, that is changes of letters, occur. Bassalygo, Gelfand, and Pinsker introduced the concept of localized errors. They assume that the encoder, who wants to encode message m, knows the t-element set E/spl sub/[n]={1,2,...,n} of positions, in which errors may occur. The encoder can make the codeword, representing m, dependent on E/spl isin//spl Escr//sub t/, the family of t-elements subsets of [n]. The authors call them a priori error pattern. The set of associated (a posteriori) errors is V(E)={e/sup n/=(e/sub 1/,...,e/sub n/)/spl isin/X/sup n/:e/sub t/=0 for t/spl notin/E}. They introduce probabilistic communication models with localized errors and determine the optimal rates of codes, if a priori error patterns or actual errors or both occur at random according to uniform distributions. There are strong connections to the theory of arbitrarily varying channels. The authors also have new coding technique for additive arbitrarily varying channels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Soft-decision decoding implementation with reduced complexity for binary block codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A simplified soft-decision decoding for binary block codes is presented, in which the time for hard-decision decoding to decode a codeword of (n, k) block code is up to n and the error performance is similar to that of the maximum likelihood decoder.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new decoding algorithm for trellis codes over groups
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A new decoding algorithm for geometrically uniform TCM schemes is proposed, based on the group properties of code sequences and trellis states, Its complexity is almost independent from the number of states of the trellis, and, for a given code, a trade-off between complexity and performance of the algorithm can be chosen.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Error correcting codes on periodically disturbed data channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The paper introduces the "periodically disturbed data channel" (PDC) and some of its characteristics from the coding theoretical point of view. After defining an error model, the error detection conditions using cyclic codes are derived. Furthermore, two methods of error correction for this error model are examined. One is the use of a multiparameter burst error correcting code, the other one applies a cyclic code based on self-dual polynomials. For both methods a decoding strategy is developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High-order spectral-null codes: constructions and bounds
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Derives upper and lower bounds on the cardinality and minimum distance of the set S(n,k) of length-n sequences with order-k spectral null at zero frequency. The authors also provide constructions of block codes that are subsets of S(n,k) with rate approaching unity as n/spl rarr//spl infin/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multidimensional MPSK trellis codes for fading channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The paper investigates the optimum code search problem of multidimensional MPSK trellis codes for fading channels. New set partitioning schemes are proposed for fading channels by using effective code length and minimum product distance as the code design criteria. Based on these set partitioning rules, a number of optimum multidimensional MPSK trellis codes have been obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Symmetry properties of deBruijn sequences
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Symmetry properties of deBruijn sequences are defined and methods for finding, symmetry groups of sets of such sequences are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Acquisition based capacity of a synchronous direct sequence spread spectrum multiple access technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In deriving the capacity of a direct sequence spread spectrum (DS/SS) multiple access system using the bit error rate (BER), it is assumed that the receiver has already achieved chip synchronisation with the spreading sequence used. In the absence of any other timing information the acquisition based capacity is also very important. It has been found that asymptotically, that is as the length N of the matched filter used to achieve the synchronization tends to infinity and pfa, the probability of acquisition failure tends to zero, the acquisition based capacity is upper bounded by N/2ln N, denoted as J/sub a/symp. However, this bound J/sub a/symp is not tight for finite N. In fact for a specified pfa, and N, the actual maximum number of users can be orders of magnitude lower than the predicted J/sub a/symp. Thus, from a practical point of view the asymptotic bound is not very useful for a given problem at hand. We formulate the acquisition based capacity for a specified pfa and N.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An optimization algorithm for estimating the storage requirements of a reduced-search decoder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A classical problem in reduced-search channel decoding has been the accurate estimation by computational or analytical means of the smallest code search that attains a set performance. The problem is particularly difficult for breadth-first decoders (i.e, decoders without balancing), that work from a fixed size storage of trellis paths. An obvious measure of performance is the overall bit error rate. An easier measure to analyze is the distance attainable in a bounded-distance decoder. If the decoder is to correct all channel noises of length or weight less than d what size storage does it need? We define an optimization problem whose solution is this maximum size, propose a solution based on a contraction mapping, and give numerical results for ordinary convolutional and partial-response codes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trellis assisted block synchronisation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A new essentially "intrinsic" synchronisation technique is introduced. Bit, symbol and block synchronisations obtained directly from the received signals, and timing intervals are derived from the output soft maximum likelihood trellis decoder which also performs error correction of the received data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On TB-SV4 based subband coding of videoconference sequences
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Presents a fixed rate, low complexity video compression scheme based on trellis based scalar-vector quantization applied to motion compensated subbands, suitable for video teleconferencing. TB-SVQ is known to asymptotically (in block length) achieve the optimal boundary gain as well as realizing a significant portion of the granular gain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On band-limited additive Gaussian noise channels in the presence of sampling jitter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: One of the topics in information theory is the study of communication through bandlimited waveform channels corrupted by Gaussian noise. In practical receiver implementations, sampling is used to obtain a digital representation of the received signal which is amenable to advanced processing. We consider information theoretic consequences of nonideal uniform sampling combined with additive Gaussian noise. In particular, we find that for Gaussian distributed waveforms, sampling jitter, just like additive noise, leads to a fundamental limit on reliable communication speed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of noisy quantized random observation coefficient AR time-series
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present a consistent, asymptotically normal estimation algorithm for the parameters of auto-regressive (AR) processes from 1-bit quantized observations. The input signal to the quantifier is the AR signal corrupted by multiplicative white Gaussian noise. Our algorithm is computationally inexpensive as it involves counting the number of occurrences of particular patterns of zeros and ones in the observation sequence and then solving a Yule-Walker type system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Construction of signal sets matched to Abelian and Non-Abelian groups
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present an algorithm for the construction of signal sets matched to abelian and non-abelian groups based on the concept of the closed d-chain. This algorithm fixes and extends the proof of the theorem by Slepian (1968) on d-chains, and extends the result of Loeliger (1991) on signal sets matched to groups.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A lower bound on the expected length of one-to-one codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Shows that the expected length of any one-to-one encoding of a discrete random variable X is at least H(X)-log (H(X)+1)-log e and that this bound is asymptotically achievable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quadrature partial response-trellis coded modulation (QPR-TCM) on fading mobile satellite channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In previous studies of Ucan et al. [1992], to improve bandwidth efficiency and error performance, partial response signalling (PRS) and trellis coded modulation (TCM) [Ungerboeck, 1982] are considered together for 4QAM and named as 6QPR-TCM. In 6QPR-TCM, there is one to many mapping from the signal set domain to the input data range. In order to solve this catastrophic case, a new non-catastrophic QPR-TCM scheme, M/6QPR-TCM is introduced. For the encoder with three units memory followed by PRS a new scheme is proposed and named as 9QPR-TCM. In fading mobile satellite channels analytical upper bound curves of the considered schemes are compared with the related 4QAM-TCM.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive rate multiple access (ARMA) for wireless multimedia communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: A challenge for personal communication system (PCS) is to provide bandwidth demanding multimedia communications such as interactive video and high quality images to portable communication terminals. Such communications, requiring a transport bit-rate in multiples of Mb/s, are readily available via fiber optics using access methods such as the asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) with a transport capacity of tens or hundreds of Mb/s. This paper proposes a new channel access, coding, and modulation scheme called adaptive rate multiple access (ARMA) over the wireless channel. ARMA is proposed to inter-network with a wired ATM network, to deal with the severe bit-rate limitations of fading and intersymbol interference (ISI), and the variable bit-rate requirements of multimedia communications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of adaptive MLSE equalization on multipath fading channels with imperfect channel estimates
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In the literature, the performance of maximum-likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) equalization on multipath fading channels is analysed under the assumption of perfect channel estimates. In reality, this condition is difficult to attain, especially for fast fading channels. It is therefore of great significance to study the performance degradation due to imperfect channel estimates. In this paper, we consider a practical MLSE equalizer in conjunction with a least mean square (LMS) channel estimator and a simple channel predictor. A new upper-bound on block error rate is derived for multipath Rayleigh fading channels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rate-distortion efficiency of subband coding with integer coefficient filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Discusses efficient image compression algorithms that are suitable for low-complexity implementation in deep space probes. Subband coding or equivalent wavelet transforms provide some advantages over traditional block transforms in terms of rate distortion performance under the mean square-error criterion and according to subjective visual evaluation. Furthermore, the possibility of choosing a desired resolution, independently in the time or frequency domain, is important to preserve the specific features that are most relevant for substantiating scientific findings. A low-complexity version of a JPEG-like algorithm based on the integer cosine transform (ICT), is being implemented in software on the Galileo spacecraft. The most promising candidate for improving the current ICT-based algorithm is a subband coding method that uses quadrature mirror filters (QMF) with lattice structure and integer coefficients. Lattice QMF filters are paraunitary perfect reconstruction (PR) filters. This provides a simple method to obtain PR filters with integer coefficients, without the need for any additional constraint to be satisfied for guaranteeing the PR property. Similarly, orthonormal wavelet transforms can be easily implemented by de signing a two-channel paraunitary QMF bank and then using a tree structure. This means that the wavelet orthonormality properties can be retained even when the coefficients are quantized or subject to certain constraints.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Learning decision rules for pattern classification under a family of probability measures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In this paper, the PAC learnability of decision rules for pattern classification under a family of probability measures is investigated. It is shown that uniform boundedness of the metric entropy of the class of decision rules is both necessary and sufficient for learnability if the family of probability measures is either compact, or contains an interior point, with respect to total variation metric. Then it is shown that learnability is preserved under finite unions of families of probability measures, and also that learnability with respect to each of a finite number of measures implies learnability with respect to the convex hull of the families of "commensurate" probability measures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An ideal theoretic approach for classifying high rate convolutional codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The authors discuss finite input convolutional codes, their corresponding properties, and some differences between these codes and infinite input convolutional codes. They also give an algebraic description of all rate n-1/n finite input convolutional codes of McMillan degree /spl les//spl alpha/ where /spl alpha/ is any positive integer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance approximation for trellis coded diversity receivers over slowly fading Rayleigh channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The well known transfer function bounding technique for trellis codes is used to obtain an approximation for the bit error rate of a trellis coded diversity receiver over a slowly fading Rayleigh channel. The approximation accommodates diversity reception through a modification of the branch labeling of the error state diagram.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiple description source coding with excess rate
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Multiple description source coding concerns situations in which the transmission of the source information is distributed over two channels at rates R/sub 1/ and R/sub 2/, respectively. When both channels are operative, the decoder receives data at rate R/sub 1/+R/sub 2/ which is used to reconstruct the source information with average distortion d/sub 0/. If one of the channels breaks down, the receiver has to base its reconstruction solely on the data available at rate either R/sub 1/ or R/sub 2/, depending on which channel is operative. This results in a higher distortion of either d/sub 1/ or d/sub 2/, respectively. The region R of all quintuples (R/sub 1/,R/sub 2/, d/sub 0/, d/sub l/, d/sub 2/) has been determined in the so-called /spl Sigma/'no excess rate' case defined by imposing the requirement R/sub 1/+R/sub 2/=R(d/sub 0/), where R(/spl middot/) is the rate-distortion function of the source. The case with excess rate in which R/sub 1/+R/sub 2/>R(d/sub 0/) is permitted seems difficult. Hence we study here a special case of the excess rate problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sequential decision making using expert advice
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Presents a theory for sequentially choosing decisions by combining the suggestions of a fixed number of experts. the author takes a game theoretic approach and attempts to do as well as the best expert under worst case assumptions. Surprisingly, it is possible to do as well as if one knows the statistics of the system in advance. The author applies these results to the problem of how to gamble on a sequence of letters drawn from a finite alphabet.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of recurrent neural networks to channel equalization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: This paper presents a recurrent neural network based channel equalizer. Simulations show that the proposed equalizer performance compares favorably with traditional ones and offers a large flexibility regarding its capability of tracking channel variations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Convergence analysis of Sato blind equalizer with discrete channel input
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The convergence properties of the Sato algorithm for a blind equalizer are analyzed when the channel input is discrete, especially M-ary pulse amplitude modulation (PAM). At first, it is shown that there exist local minima in the mean cost function of Sato algorithm for M-ary PAM input, and then the effect of increasing M on the size of the attractive region of each local minimum is analyzed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust/lossy discretization in CDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Robust/lossy discretization (RLD) alleviates the synchronization problem for code-division multiple-access (CDMA) systems at the expense of a small performance penalty. From the received signal, a low-pass filter removes high-frequency components that bear little information about the transmitted data. Discretization is achieved by sampling the resulting signal. To evaluate the performance of RLD, an expression for the sum information rate is derived. RLD is shown to be less sensitive to the spectral properties of the transmitted signal than matched-filter discretization and works well in CDMA systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polynomial of correctable patterns of product codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Product codes have a poor minimum distance, but an efficient low-complexity decoding algorithm. To measure the performance of a decoder, like Reddy-Robinson's for product codes, which decode error patterns beyond half the minimum distance, we use the notion of equivalent diameter of the decoding region [4]. We produce here a bound for the performance of product code which is, for the considered example, far below the simulated performance but still above the performance of known BCH codes with same parameters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bounds for non-binary synchronization error correction codes and their construction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We first show asymptotic bounds for non-binary synchronization error correction codes which count symbol errors in the Hamming metric. We next propose a new metric which counts symbol error in the Lee metric and show asymptotic bounds for the synchronization error correction codes. We finally show the effectiveness of the proposed metric by giving several code examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Large sets of code-sequences with good correlation properties derived from character products
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: In this paper we investigate large families of polyphase sequences which can be expressed as product of an additive and a multiplicative character. The construction of a family with size M=N(N+2) and maximum magnitude of the periodic correlation function /spl theta/~/sub max//spl les/2/spl radic/N+1 is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Linear codes over cyclic groups
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Investigates the structure of linear block codes defined over cyclic groups Z/sub q/ (q=p/sup L/ with p prime), i.e., of the subgroups of (Z/sub q/)/sup n/. Bounds on the Euclidean distance of block-coded modulation schemes associated with these codes are also provided, along with some examples of these schemes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Information rates by over-sampling the sign of a bandlimited process
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We are interested in /spl Iscr/ the average mutual information between the signal's input samples and the binary output samples normalized to a Nyquist interval (that is per n binary samples). We focus on the achievable values of /spl Iscr/. We construct via the Hadamard factorization a bounded Zakai bandlimited process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On Viterbi decoding of high rate convolutional codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We present a new soft decision decoding method for partial unit memory (PUM) codes. The method exploits the linearity of the parallel transitions in the trellis associated with such a code. We provide bounds on the number of operations per decoded bit, and show that this number is dependent on the weight hierarchy of the linear block codes associated with the parallel transitions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A stochastic model for image segmentation involving constrained least squares estimation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The aim of the paper is to outline a layered statistical image model suitable for unsupervised image segmentation. The segment internal texture signal is described based on its spatial frequency representation while the image partition is modelled as a sample of a Gibbs/Markov random field. The most likely segmentation is estimated using a maximum a posteriori (MAP) formulation with the unknown parameters being determined by constrained least squares (CLS) estimation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A/sup 2/-codes and codes for the rank metric
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Simmons (1990) has introduced an extended authentication model where caution is taken both against deceptions from an outsider (opponent) and against some forms of deception from the insiders (transmitter and receiver). Codes for this model are called authentication codes with arbitration, or simply A/sup 2/ codes. A new construction of authentication codes with arbitration is proposed, which uses codes for the rank metric.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Decoding of a Cartesian product set with a constraint on an additive cost; fixed-rate entropy-coded vector quantization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The authors consider a discrete set of points A composed of K=|A| elements. A non-negative cost c(a) is associated with each element a/spl isin/A. The n-fold Cartesian product of A is dented as {A}/sup n/. The cost of an n-fold element a=(a/sub 0/, ..., a/sub n-1/)/spl isin/{A}/sup n/ is equal to: c(a)=/spl Sigma//sub i/ c(a/sub i/). The authors select a subset of the n-fold elements, S/sub n//spl isin/{A}/sup n/, with a cost less than or equal to a given value c/sub max/. They refer to A as the constituent subset. They consider another set of n-tuples X/sub n/ denoted as the input set. A non-negative distance is defined between each x=(x/sub 0/, ..., x/sub n-1/)/spl isin/X/sub n/, and each s=(s/sub 0/, ..., s/sub n-1/)/spl isin/S/sub n/. The distance between x/sub i/ and s/sub i/ is denoted as d(x/sub i/,s/sub i/). The distance between x and s is equal to: d(x,s)=/spl Sigma//sub i/d(x/sub i/, s/sub i/). Decoding of an element x/spl isin/X/sub n/ is to find the element s/spl isin/S/sub n/ which has the minimum distance to x. A major application of this decoding problem is in fixed-rate entropy-coded vector quantization where A is the set of reconstruction vectors of a vector quantizer and cost is equivalent to self-information.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the cost of universality of block codes for individual sequences
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Consider a rate R block code of size k that achieves minimum distortion for a given individual input sequence. Such a code obviously depends on the input sequence. The author seek a universal (sequence-independent) rate R' block code of size l (l>k), which guarantees a distortion not higher than that of the above optimal sequence-dependent block code. They ask the question of the cost of universality: what is the best achievable rate R' as a function of the block length l of the universal code such that the above task could be fulfilled? They provide achievable bounds that characterize this optimal rate.
