abstract: We propose a simple analytical upper bound on the pairwise error probability of random error correcting codes when used over a Rayleigh fading channel with exponential time-correlation. The results are derived under the assumptions of coherent demodulation, soft decision decoding, and perfect channel state information.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MPSK coded modulations for the Rayleigh fading channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The error performance of a modulation code over the Rayleigh fading channel depends primarily on its minimum symbol distance, minimum product distance, and path multiplicity. It depends on the minimum squared Euclidean distance to a lesser degree. The paper is concerned with construction of MPSK modulation codes for the Rayleigh fading channel. Several construction methods are presented. Codes constructed by these methods achieve good error performance with reduced decoding complexity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Continuity and consistency of greedy growing for tree-structured vector quantizers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Tree structured vector quantizers (TSVQ) provide a computationally efficient, variable rate method of compressing vector-valued data. In applications, the problem of designing a TSVQ from empirical training data is critical. A widely used approach to the design problem is the greedy growing algorithm, which produces a labeled binary tree one node at a time by optimizing a simple splitting criterion at each stage. While the greedy growing algorithm is well understood from an experimental standpoint, there has been little theory to support its use, or to examine its behavior on large training sets. This talk presents the results of a rigorous analysis of the greedy growing algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On Massey's bound on the worst-case probability of undetected error
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The author shows that for a binary linear code, Massey's bound on the worst-case probability of undetected error can be improved by a factor /spl radic/n.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A constructive code reaching capacity 1 for the multiple-access collision channel with multiplicity feedback
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: Pippenger [1981] showed in a probabilistic way that the capacity of a collision channel with multiplicity feedback is one. The present authors give a constructive proof of this result.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Asymptotic capacity of multi-receiver networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: We formulate a notion of asymptotic capacity in bits/sec for a sequence of multi-user, multi-receiver networks. Using this notion of bit rate capacity, we define a dual notion of capacity in users per Hz and prove that the capacity region is convex. We consider an application of this result to mobile radio.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Permutation coding of images using cosine transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
abstract: The paper presents the concept of permutation coding (PC), which has typical applications for low bit-rate image compressing and coding.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
